newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias details actions by creditors.
newsitem.headline: Victorias details actions by creditors.

text.p: Sugar firm Victorias Milling Co Inc on Tuesday gave details of the actions taken by some of its creditors after the company sought a moratorium on principal payments of debts amounting to $192 million.
In a statement to the Philippine Stock Exchange, the company said that Land Bank of the Philippines initiated foreclosure proceedings against its marketing arm North Negros Marketing Co Inc.

Separately, two other creditors Dao Heng Bank and Bank of the Philippine Islands filed civil suits against the company for sums of money/damages arising from alleged refined sugar delivery orders (RSDOs).
The complainants said the RSDO's, which were offered as collaterals to their loans, were not supported by physical stocks.
Last week, Victorias was granted a reprieve by the Securities and Exchange Commission which suspended payments on its debts.
Victorias also listed measures it was taking to turn around the company.
It was reducing its workforce by 51 percent to 2,148 people at a cost of 496 million pesos. The savings after the retrenchments would amount to 228 million pesos, it said.
It also gave details of how operating efficiences would be improved. -- Manila newsroom (632) 841 8934
